title: 15m OBV leads price: buy a fresh 48-hour OBV high while price sits within 1.5% below its 48-hour high
ex_ante_rule: Chart 15m, closed bars only. A signal at the close of bar t fills at the open of bar t+1. Spot, long only, one open position per pair, whole balance. DEFINITIONS: OBV(i) = OBV(i-1) + volume(i) if close(i) > close(i-1), OBV(i-1) - volume(i) if close(i) < close(i-1), OBV(i-1) if equal (raw cumulative, no smoothing; only differences and window comparisons are used, so the start level does not matter). OBVMAX(t) = max OBV over bars t-192..t-1; OBVMIN(t) = min OBV over bars t-192..t-1 (192 bars = 48 h, current bar excluded). HH(t) = highest high of bars t-192..t-1 (current bar excluded). L10(t) = lowest low of bars t-9..t (10 bars including the signal bar). FILTER (closed 1h bars only, merged with merge_informative_pair so that only the last COMPLETED 1h bar is visible): 1h close > EMA(50) of 1h closes. ENTRY at the close of bar t when ALL hold: (1) OBV(t) > OBVMAX(t); (2) close(t) < HH(t); (3) close(t) >= 0.985 x HH(t); (4) close(t) > open(t); (5) 1h filter true; (6) no open position on this pair; (7) cooldown: at least 16 completed 15m bars since the last exit on this pair; (8) fewer than 3 trades already opened on this pair during the UTC calendar day of the open of bar t+1; (9) R = close(t) - L10(t) with 0.008 <= R/close(t) <= 0.03 (else skip). Store at entry: STOP = L10(t), TARGET = close(t) + 1.5 x R. Both are fixed prices, never moved. EXITS: STOP, intrabar: when low touches STOP, sell at STOP (implemented as a constant per-trade stop distance (entry_fill - STOP)/entry_fill set at entry, not trailed; the native static stoploss is -0.04 as a backstop only). TAKE-PROFIT, intrabar: when high touches TARGET, sell at TARGET (constant per-trade ROI (TARGET - entry_fill)/entry_fill; if it is <= 0 the trade exits at the first bar). If stop and target are both touched in one bar, the stop is assumed. EARLY EXIT: if OBV(t) < OBVMIN(t) at the close of any bar while in the trade, sell at the next open. TIME EXIT: sell at the open of the bar 48 bars (12 h) after the entry bar. No trailing stop, no pyramiding, no other filters. Warm-up: 2000 bars (15m; = 500 closed 1h bars, 10x the EMA(50) period for recursive stability; longest 15m lookback is 193 bars).
rationale: Granville's on-balance volume premise: volume leads price. When OBV prints a fresh 48-hour high while price is still capped within 1.5% under its 48-hour high, signed volume is piling onto up bars without price breaking out, i.e. a buyer is absorbing offers parked below resistance. The counterparties are holders taking profit below the old high and range mean-reverters selling into resistance; once their offers are absorbed, the high breaks and breakout bots and stop orders add fuel, and this rule is already long below that crowd's entry. The bullish close (close > open) confirms the up-pressure on the signal bar and the 1h close above EMA(50) is the single higher-timeframe activity/direction filter (option d), fixed in advance, keeping the rule out of falling markets where the 2022-2024 momentum rules lost. In a range the rule mostly stays flat (price far from highs) or exits early on an OBV 48-hour low. Expected frequency: about one qualifying signal per pair per day before the risk band and filter, roughly 150-350 trades per year per pair after them. The stop is at least 0.8% and at most 3% away, the target 1.5R, so a winner grosses at least 1.2% and the average absolute move per trade should be around 1-2%, well above the 0.30% base / 0.45% conservative round trip (cost under 0.4R even at the minimum stop). All numbers are taken from idea I-095 as written, fixed before any test.
novelty_vs_tried: No tried hypothesis uses OBV or any cumulative signed-volume extreme. Breakout families (WeeklyBreakoutRegime, SessionOpeningRangeBreakout, HourlyWilliamsVolBreakout, MoneyFlowBreakout H-079) buy AFTER price clears a high; this rule buys BEFORE the price breakout, requiring price to still be below the 48-hour high, with the volume-flow line making the new high instead. H-079 used CMF (a bounded, close-location-weighted ratio) plus a price breakout on 1h; volume-spike families (VolumeSpikeCrashRebound, VolumeConditionedReversal, USOpenVolumeContinuation) use single-bar volume bursts, not accumulated signed volume over 48 hours. The stop is structural (10-bar low, constrained to 0.8-3%) with a 1.5R target and a 12-hour time exit.
data_visible_at_proposal: No price data inspected; only the H-112 context file (exploration-only learnings digest) and the validation protocol, as of 2026-11-11
